chapter: The 1940s: small groups, Teddy Wilson and Ethel Waters
title: Trio at the Vanguard, then Barney Bigard's group
summary: He took a trio into the Vanguard for several months, twice. After Wilson, Barney Bigard offered Thomas a job at Fat Man's on 155th Street, and arranged around his own college dates. He calls it a terrific group.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Think you went from there to the Vanguard. Didn't you? That's where you took a small group to the Vanguard.
Yes, it was. I took a group to the Vanguard.
You took a trio into the Vanguard, right?
I don't know but we had a nice little deal down there for maybe three or four months and we came on back and did three or four months again.
Yeah, he's got that here. Then he's got you in with Barney Bigard at the Onyx.
Oh, that's a jump really. No, I left Teddy and went to Barney. One of the most pleasant experiences I ever had working with the guys.
This was after he left ?, of course.

Yeah, it could have been around that time. ... I was going uptown one night on the subway so I saw Barney; I don't think Barney knew me that well. He knew I played trumpet. So he says, What you doing? Well, things were happening very good for us at that time. Babe and I were doing some college really dates and so I didn't want to be pinned down. And, he said Why don't you come on out and go in the band with me? I said, That's a helluva offer from a guy like you. I mean I've got some things I've got to do. So we talked about it. He said, We're at Fat Man's, right on the corner, 155th Street, we got to talking about it and I told him my ... He said, We can
arrange that. You got to get off. What the hell, we can arrange that. No problem. So I worked for him about three months. We had a terrific group.
